title: Reefer Cargo Services: when an excursion earns a credit and how the credit is calculated
content:
## Scope

This clause of **Reefer Cargo Services** decides whether a recorded temperature excursion earns the customer an excursion credit on the reefer service, and how much that credit is.

## Rule

1. A service earns an excursion credit when an excursion **lasted at least** the tier's credit threshold, the tier's threshold being above 0, and the excursion was **not** caused by:
   - the shipper's own instruction,
   - a set point outside the commodity's needs, or
   - cargo loaded above the set point.
2. The credit is the tier's credit percentage of the **credit basis**, rounded to the cent, and never more than the tier's credit cap. The credit references the excursion record it compensates.
3. The credit basis is the total of the amounts of the service's charge records under the credit-basis charges, over the life of the service up to the credit date.
4. An excursion credit is a **service credit only**. Loss of cargo value is not compensated by it; that is a cargo claim under the company's claims rules.

## Tier table

| Tier | Credit threshold (continuous excursion minutes) | Credit percentage of the basis | Credit cap per service |
|---|---|---|---|
| AHL Reefer Standard | 0 (earns no credit) | 0 percent | 0.00 USD |
| AHL Reefer Monitored | 240 | 25 percent | 250.00 USD |
| AHL Reefer Cold Treatment | 120 | 50 percent | 750.00 USD |
| AHL Reefer Controlled Atmosphere | 180 | 50 percent | 900.00 USD |
| AHL Reefer Pharma GDP | 60 | 100 percent | 2500.00 USD |
| AHL Reefer Superfreezer | 240 | 50 percent | 1500.00 USD |

**Credit-basis charges (identical on every tier):** terminal plug-in and monitoring fees, the remote monitoring fee, the cold treatment fee, the controlled atmosphere surcharge, the GDP handling fee and the superfreezer surcharge. Charges not on this list, such as pre-trip inspection fees, setting change fees, the late request fee and the cancellation fee, do not enter the basis.

## Calculation order

1. Total the service's charges under the credit-basis charges up to the credit date.
2. Multiply that total by the tier's credit percentage.
3. Round the result to the cent.
4. Take the lower of the rounded result and the tier's credit cap. That is the credit.

## Worked examples (hypothetical amounts)

> **AHL Reefer Monitored**, excursion of 255 continuous minutes, no excluded cause. Basis: plug-in fees of 165.00 USD and 60.00 USD plus a remote monitoring fee of 264.33 USD, a total of 489.33 USD. 25 percent of 489.33 USD is 122.3325 USD, rounded to 122.33 USD. That is below the 250.00 USD cap, so the credit is 122.33 USD.

> **AHL Reefer Controlled Atmosphere**, excursion of 200 minutes, no excluded cause, basis 2,100.00 USD. 50 percent is 1,050.00 USD; the cap is 900.00 USD, so the credit is 900.00 USD.

> **AHL Reefer Cold Treatment**, excursion of 120 minutes, basis 1,234.56 USD. The excursion meets the threshold exactly; 50 percent is 617.28 USD, below the 750.00 USD cap, so the credit is 617.28 USD.

## Threshold and cause boundary cases

| Tier | Excursion | Cause | Credit earned? |
|---|---|---|---|
| AHL Reefer Monitored | 240 minutes | Not an excluded cause | Yes: at least the threshold |
| AHL Reefer Monitored | 225 minutes | Not an excluded cause | No: below the threshold |
| AHL Reefer Pharma GDP | 90 minutes | A set point outside the commodity's needs | No: excluded cause |
| AHL Reefer Superfreezer | 300 minutes | Cargo loaded warmer than the set point | No: excluded cause |
| AHL Reefer Standard | Any length | Any | No: the tier's threshold is 0 |

## Basis Q&A

**Wrong reading:** "The credit is the percentage of all charges on the service." **Correct basis:** only charges under the credit-basis list count.

**The customer asks for the value of spoiled fruit.** The excursion credit is a service credit only; loss of cargo value is a cargo claim.
